prompts.evidence: Fails supported_by_section. Supported ideas: each light has its own pattern and sailors count the flashes (d02-p006, 'every light on the coast had its own pattern, and that sailors counted the flashes'); Gannet Rock's pattern is unique (d02-p006, 'one white flash every ten seconds; no other light on the coast did the same'). Unsupported claim: 'made by a lens with four bright panels that turned once every forty seconds'. No paragraph of this section states it; d02-p005 describes the lens only as 'built from rings of cut glass' bending the flame 'into one narrow beam'. The panels and the forty-second turn are in d02-p008, section s0002 ('the gears turned the lens once every forty seconds, and its four bright panels gave four flashes on each turn'). The prompt itself is answerable from d02-p006 and does not telegraph the answer.

Idea 1 (he steered by the sound of the horn alone, following its pattern): d03-p009, 'He had steered by the sound of the horn alone— two blasts, then silence, then two blasts again'. Idea 2 (until the boat grounded below the tower): d03-p009, 'until his boat grounded on the shingle below the tower'. The answer calls it the 'fog horn'; the section says 'the horn' on 'the ninth night of fog', so this follows directly. The prompt does not mention sound or the horn.

Idea 1 (the cause is phosphorescence, light from tiny living creatures when the water is disturbed): d03-p010, 'phosphorescence, the light made by tiny living creatures when the water is disturbed'. Idea 2 (not dangerous): d03-p011, 'It was not, said Dr. Vane'. Idea 3 (a sign of plankton, hence fish): d03-p011, 'a sign that the water was full of plankton, and where there was plankton there would be fish'. Nothing is taken from the endnote d05-n002. The prompt names only the green light, which is the thing to be explained, and asks two closely linked parts.

Single idea (never go to sea in November without oars, however good the engine): d03-p013, 'she gave him one piece of advice: never put to sea in November without oars, however good the engine'. The answer adds nothing from the endnote d05-n003. It is close to the text's wording but short and plain enough that a reader recalling 'always carry oars, even with a good engine' can mark themselves Correct. The prompt does not mention oars or the engine.
